children: DP World, rated Baa2 with a stable outlook by Moody's and BBB+ with a stable outlook by Fitch, has mandated banks to arrange a global investor roadshow ahead of a planned dual-tranche bond offering comprising euro-denominated green notes and USD conventional notes.

The Dubai-based ports and logistics operator appointed Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Barclays, Citi, Deutsche Bank, Emirates NBD Capital, First Abu Dhabi Bank, HSBC, J.P. Morgan, Mashreq, Standard Chartered Bank and Societe Generale as joint lead managers and joint bookrunners for the transaction. Citi is coordinating the roadshow.
DP World plans to issue benchmark-sized six-year euro-denominated Reg S green notes and benchmark-sized 10-year USD-denominated Reg S notes under its $10 billion Global Medium Term Note Programme.
The logistics giant is expected to use the euro tranche to finance or refinance eligible green projects in line with its sustainable finance framework.
Recent issuances by the group include a $1.5 billion green sukuk issued in late 2025.
(Writing by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Dubai’s DP World mandates EUR, USD bond sale
